Re-gated docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-021.md (branch feature/WF02-REQ-021, commit 906bd78) after TEST-DESIGNER's rework1 (handoffs/WF02-REQ-021/step-03-test-designer-rework1.json) addressing this gate's prior FAIL (handoffs/WF02-REQ-021/step-03b-test-design-validator.json, MAJOR on AC2b's cross-process fixture collision). Read the reworked spec file directly, ran `git show 906bd78 -- docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-021.md` to see the exact diff, and independently re-checked the new AC2b section against the real schema and the codebase's own established fixture idiom -- not TEST-DESIGNER's result.summary.

Diff scope confirmed surgical: `git show 906bd78 --stat` touches only docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-021.md and the new step-03-test-designer-rework1.json handoff file. Within REQ-021.md, the diff's two hunks are (1) AC2b's section body (lines ~221-284) and (2) the AC2 coverage-table row's description text -- no other AC section, harness note, or unrelated coverage-table row was touched.

Collision fix verified genuinely closes the gap (checks 1-3 of this gate's task):

1. No re-invocation instruction remains. The new AC2b text states explicitly, in bold, that order-independence is checked as '3 loop iterations inside this one script invocation (one process, run once)' and explicitly rules out re-invoking the whole script 3 times as separate `npx tsx` processes -- the exact mechanism the prior FAIL was about is gone, not just downgraded.
2. Fixture disjointness re-derived directly, not trusted from prose: the loop declares a script-local `tieIterSeq` counter incremented once per iteration (0->1->2->3), producing chapter codes `r21a2-tie-1`/`-2`/`-3` (distinct string literals per iteration, and distinct from AC2a's `r21a2script` and AC2c's default `seedChapter()` code), a fresh `eventIdN` per iteration tied to that iteration's own chapter, and two fresh users per iteration via tg_ids derived from the same counter (`1000000450 + tieIterSeq*2` and `+1`), which are pairwise disjoint across all 3 iterations by construction (1000000452/453, 1000000454/455, 1000000456/457 for iterations 1/2/3). Cross-checked this counter-based idiom against the real, already-committed pattern in apps/bot/src/domain/registration.db.test.ts lines 52-54 (`chapterSeq`/`userSeq`/`tgSeq` module-level counters, incremented once per `seedChapter()`/`seedUser()` call) and lines 56-83 (the helper bodies) -- the new AC2b code is a faithful instance of the same established idiom, and since it is a single in-process counter (not a fixed literal, and not restarted between iterations), collision is structurally impossible within the run. This directly answers the prior FAIL's root cause: the old design's fixed literal codes/tg_ids were the problem, and the new design replaced them with a monotonic in-process counter -- the actual fix, not a workaround.
3. Single-process confirmed independently: verified apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts lines 54 (`chapters_code_unique` on `chapters.code`) and 94 (`users_tg_id_unique` on `users.tgId`) still exist unchanged -- these are exactly the constraints the old design would have violated on process re-invocation. Since the new design never restarts the process between iterations (one `npx tsx` invocation, a `for` loop inside it), these unique indexes are never asked to accept a value already committed by an earlier iteration of the same run -- module-level counters in a single Node process only ever increase, so no two iterations can produce the same code/tg_id even accidentally.

Property-preservation verified (check 4 of this gate's task) -- the fix did not weaken what AC2b proves:

4. Each loop iteration still performs a genuine two-row `INSERT ... VALUES (...), (...)` with byte-identical `createdAt` (the same literal `2026-11-02T00:00:00.000Z` every iteration -- only the surrounding fixture identities vary, never the tie itself) into a wholly fresh, otherwise-empty event (`eventIdN`, unique per iteration, with zero pre-existing registrations). The insert statement's shape, the `.returning()` call, and the post-hoc lexicographic `id` sort used to predict the tie-break winner are all byte-identical to the pre-fix version -- the loop wraps the existing mechanism unchanged, it does not alter how the insert is issued or add anything (index hints, explicit ORDER BY, a warmed/pre-touched connection) that could bias Postgres's row-return order in a particular direction. Since nothing pins insertion-order-vs-return-order and each iteration's event starts empty, Postgres remains free to return the two rows in either order on each of the 3 independent iterations -- the exact nondeterminism source AC2b exists to prove the tie-break is immune to is still genuinely exercised 3 times, not accidentally biased toward always matching insertion order. Confirmed the expected/pass-condition prose was updated consistently (`tieResults` array of 3 entries, each must read `{lowerIdPosition: 1, higherIdPosition: 2}`, any iteration failing is a FAIL) -- no weakening of the assertion (e.g. no 'at least 2 of 3' escape hatch, no averaging).

AC1/AC2a/AC2c/AC3/AC4 confirmed untouched (check 5): re-read AC2a (lines 157-219), AC2c (286-315), AC3 (319-349), AC4 (353-418) in the current file and cross-checked their content against the diff hunks from `git show 906bd78` above -- these sections are byte-identical to the pre-fix version already reviewed and PASSed on in the prior gate's other findings (which this re-gate does not need to re-litigate, since the diff proves they were not touched). The only coverage-table row changed is AC2's description text, updated to describe the loop-iteration mechanism -- consistent with the new AC2b prose, no contradiction introduced.

No new 'TODO' found. Every case in the reworked section remains precise enough to run without judgment (exact loop count, exact counter formula, exact expected object shape, exact FAIL condition). Single-issue fix confirmed scoped exactly to what the prior FAIL required; no new issue found. PASS.
